initialContact.message: I'm getting my driver's license next month and my dad is giving me his old car (2010 Toyota worth maybe 3,000€). I looked at car insurance and it's insanely expensive for 18-year-old! Quotes are 1,200-1,800€/year! I only make 650€/month. Do I really need full insurance or can I just get the minimum legal requirement? What even is the difference?

problemContext.currentSituation: Vocational student getting first car, shocked by young driver insurance costs
problemContext.emotionalState: excited about car, shocked by insurance cost, confused about options

idealAdvice: Young driver insurance shock is real - everyone goes through this!
Finnish car insurance requirements:
LEGALLY REQUIRED: Liikennevakuutus (traffic insurance / third-party liability)
- Covers damage you cause to OTHER people/cars
- Cost for 18-year-old: ~800-1,000€/year minimum
- Cannot drive without this - illegal and huge fines
OPTIONAL: Kaskovakuutus (comprehensive insurance)
- Covers damage to YOUR car (theft, vandalism, accidents you cause)
- Cost: Additional 400-800€/year
- Total: 1,200-1,800€/year (what you were quoted)
For your situation (2010 Toyota worth 3,000€):
Full kasko insurance: Costs 400-800€/year to insure car worth 3,000€
If you total the car: Insurance pays maybe 2,500€ (after deductible)
Math: Paying 600€/year to insure 3,000€ asset
In 5 years: You've paid 3,000€ in kasko premiums = value of car
Recommendation for old car + young driver:
Get liikennevakuutus ONLY (legally required ~800-1,000€/year)
Skip kasko insurance (car too old to justify cost)
If you crash and total YOUR car: It's a loss, but you're out 3,000€ not 15,000€
Your dad gave you car for free - if it's destroyed, painful but not financial crisis
Budget impact:
800€/year = ~67€/month for required insurance
Plus fuel: ~150€/month if driving to school/work
Plus maintenance: ~50€/month average
Total car ownership: ~270€/month on 650€ income = tight but doable
Tips to lower cost:
- Add yourself to parent's insurance if possible (cheaper as 'additional driver')
- Higher deductible = lower premium
- Limited mileage option if not driving much
- Shop around: IF, Pohjola, LähiTapiola have very different young driver rates
As you get older: Insurance drops dramatically (22, 25, 30 year marks)
Drive safely first years: No accidents = no claims = lower rates later
commonMistakes: Not clearly explaining difference between required vs optional insurance
Recommending full kasko for old car (waste of money)
Not acknowledging young driver rates ARE genuinely expensive
Failing to break down total monthly car ownership costs
Not explaining insurance costs drop as he gets older
